articles.headline: Jaylen Waddle’s quiet Denver debut flips into a 138-yard day in a Broncos' 20-13 comeback over Jags
articles.description: — Jaylen Waddle and Jonah Coleman's led a big second-half comeback by the Denver Broncos, who snapped the Jacksonville Jaguars' nine-game regular-season winning streak with a 20-13 victory Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ワドルの静かなデンバーデビューが一変、138ヤードの活躍でブロンコスがジャガーズに20-13で逆転勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイレン・ワドルとジョナ・コールマンがデンバー・ブロンコスの後半の大逆転劇を牽引し、日曜日に行われた試合でジャクソンビル・ジャガーズのレギュラーシーズン連勝記録を9で止め、20-13で勝利を収めた。
articles.body:
DENVER -- — Jaylen Waddle and Jonah Coleman's led a big second-half comeback by the Denver Broncos, who snapped the Jacksonville Jaguars' nine-game regular-season winning streak with a 20-13 victory Sunday.


              After catching just one pass for 2 yards in his Denver debut, Waddle had eight catches for 138 yards and Coleman's 3-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter capped a 17-0 Broncos blitz after they'd fallen behind 13-3 early in the third quarter.


              After allowing a field goal to open the second half, the Broncos (1-1) responded with a field goal, a 7-yard touchdown toss from Bo Nix to Nate Adkins and Coleman's first career TD, which came with 7:21 remaining after starter J.K. Dobbins had left with a hamstring injury.


              The Jaguars (1-1), who had won their past nine regular-season games and by a combined 177 points, including a 34-20 win in Denver last December, punted on their next possession and the Broncos chewed up final 4:41 of game clock with Coleman running six times for 33 yards.


              Trevor Lawrence led Jacksonville on three scoring drives as the Jaguars built a 13-3 lead on Bhayshul Tuten's 1-yard touchdown run and two field goals by Cam Little, from 44 and 23 yards.


              Little was wide left on a 54-yard try in the fourth quarter before Denver's go-ahead touchdown drive. 


              The Broncos tightened up things on defense after missing a whopping 28 tackles in their season-opening loss at Kansas City six days earlier and they finally got the ball into Waddle's hands.


              The Broncos got off to a slow start, failing to punch the ball into the end zone after Waddle's 49-yard reception at the 1 in the first half, settling instead for Wil Lutz's 20-yard field goal.


              And Nix was picked off in the end zone by Jourdan Lewis, which led to Little's 44-yarder as time expired, giving Jacksonville a 10-3 halftime lead.


              The Jaguars stalled at the Denver 5-yard line on the opening drive of the second half and Little's 23-yarder made it 13-3. 


              The Jaguars caught a big break on the game's opening drive when an illegal contact flag on cornerback Riley Moss negated a strip-sack by Nik Bonitto and recovery by Alex Singleton deep in Jacksonville territory.


              Mile High comeback
              Tim Tebow returned to Empower Field at Mile High for the first time since throwing an 80-yard touchdown pass to the late Demaryius Thomas on the first play of overtime against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Jan. 8, 2012.


              The former Broncos QB and Jacksonville native served as the Broncos' alumni flag planter and was recognized as the Broncos’ “Legend of the Game” for their home opener.


              Up next
              Jaguars: host the New England Patriots on Sunday.


              Broncos: host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night.


              ------

articles.headline: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes
articles.description: Rounding up all top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
articles.headlineJa: トラビス・ケルシーとパトリック・マホームズを筆頭とするNFL第2週のベスト私服入場スタイル
articles.descriptionJa: リーグ各地から、試合前やスタジアムのトンネルに登場した注目ファッションをまとめて紹介。
articles.body:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals' defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

The source was cornerback DJ Turner II's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

"I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king. This Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

Sunday night drip

Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce showed up in style with a Louis Vuitton collarless jacket and matching belt. His teammate, Patrick Mahomes, rocked Adidas from head to toe with Oakley sunglasses.

Here are the top fits ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

Sunday afternoon arrivals

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens kept it simple up top, with a pop of color below for his arrival ahead of a divisional game against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Pickens wore a solid black T-shirt, multicolored striped shorts, and purple-and-black Nike Dunks on the feet.

Here are more notable arrivals from the 4 p.m. slate:

Best of 1 p.m. arrivals

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield was dressed to impress, arriving for a home game against his former team, the Cleveland Browns. Mayfield wore a cream polo with khaki and green striped and white shoes.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson wore a red letterman jacket and loose-fit khaki pants ahead of a road matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Here are some of the other memorable fits from Sunday's 1 p.m. slate:

Thursday night's best fit

To kick off Week 2, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb arrived in a plaid Archival button-down shirt paired with dark denim jeans.

articles.headline: 49ers score TDs on 1st 5 drives to beat the Dolphins 35-13
articles.description: — Christian McCaffrey became the fourth-fastest player in the Super Bowl era with 100 career touchdowns, Brock Purdy played a near-perfect game and the San Francisco 49ers overwhelmed the
articles.headlineJa: 49ersが最初の5ドライブすべてでタッチダウンを決め、ドルフィンズを35-13で破る
articles.descriptionJa: クリスチャン・マキャフリーがスーパーボウル時代で通算100タッチダウンに史上4番目の早さで到達し、ブロック・パーディがほぼ完璧なプレーを見せるなど、サンフランシスコ・49ersが相手を圧倒した。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- — Christian McCaffrey became the fourth-fastest player in the Super Bowl era with 100 career touchdowns, Brock Purdy played a near-perfect game and the San Francisco 49ers overwhelmed the Miami Dolphins 35-13 on Sunday.


              The 49ers (2-0) showed no signs of fatigue after beating the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 in the opener in Australia and began the season with back-to-back wins of at least 20 points for the first time in franchise history.


              They scored touchdowns on their first five drives and dominated the Dolphins (0-2), who spent the week since losing the opener in Las Vegas by practicing in nearby Napa.


              Avoiding the travel was little help to an overmatched Miami team that came into the season with a record of more than $180 million in dead money on the salary cap.


              Purdy went 20 for 22 for 287 yards, two touchdown passes and one TD run, completing 18 straight passes at one point. He connected on a 12-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle and a 6-yarder to Kyle Juszczyk on the first two drives of the third quarter to break the game open.


              McCaffrey scored on a pair of 1-yard runs to give him 100 touchdowns in 114 games, with only LaDainian Tomlinson (89 games), Emmitt Smith (93) and Shaun Alexander (96) getting their faster in the Super Bowl era.


              Malik Willis went 14 for 23 for 197 yards for Miami but took four sacks and was unable to lead a touchdown drive until his 77-yard pass to Ryan Miller with 2:30 remaining in the game.


              Both defenses struggled to get off the field in the first half with the main difference being the Niners finished off their drives with touchdowns. Riley Patterson missed a 51-yard field goal on Miami's opening drive and the Dolphins settled for two field goals in the red zone on their other two possessions in the first half.


              San Francisco got in the end zone with McCaffrey scoring on a 1-yard run and Purdy on a 2-yard run on the two drives for the 49ers, who led 14-6 at the half. 


              Injuries
              Dolphins: RB Jaylen Wright (stinger) left in the first half. ... WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) left in the second half.


              49ers: WR Demarcus Robinson (right ankle) left the game in the second quarter and didn't return. ... WR Mike Evans left in the second half with a hip injury. ... DT James Thompson Jr. (ankle) also left the game.


              Up next
              Dolphins: Host Kansas City on Sunday.


              49ers: Host Arizona on Sunday.


              ------

articles.headline: Christian Pulisic starts, gets first Milan goal of 2026 in win
articles.description: AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: クリスチャン・プリシッチが先発、勝利を収めた試合で2026年初のミランでのゴールを記録
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランは日曜日、サン・シーロでレッチェに3-0で勝利し、セリエAでの無敗記録を伸ばしました。
articles.body:
AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.

Christian Pulisic fired Ruben Amorim's side ahead early on before second-half goals from Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira wrapped up the win.

Milan now go into the international break fifth in the standings thanks to their third win of the campaign alongside two draws.

Lecce looked to strike in the opening stages as Joel Monteiro and Ivan Ilic both went close, but Milan took the lead in the 14th minute through Pulisic.

A brilliant piece of skill saw the United States striker coolly bring down Strahinja Pavlovic's cross-field pass with a single touch before moving the ball onto his left foot and firing into the bottom corner.

The goal was Pulisic's first for Milan of the calendar year after his red-hot start to the 2025 campaign came to a screeching halt in 2026. The U.S. star was not selected by Mauricio Pochettino for the squad that will play four friendlies in the upcoming international window.

Pulisic had made two other appearances with Milan this season in all competitions, coming off the bench in both at halftime. His last goal for Milan had been in December 2025 in a league win over Verona and he scored once for the U.S. in a friendly against Senegal before the start of the 2026 World Cup.

"It hasn't been an easy year," Pulisic said after the game. "I'm happy about the goal today, but right now all that matters is to keep winning."

Milan had won only one home game since March and was booed off the field in a 2-0 home loss to Benfica in the Europa League on Wednesday.

Mike Maignan was called into action to make the save from Kialonda Gaspar, and before the break Milan went close in quick succession as Koni De Winter nodded wide before Pavlovic's effort was stopped by Wladimiro Falcone.

Pervis Estupiñán had a shot blocked after the restart, but Milan doubled their advantage 61 minutes in through Rabiot, who completed a team goal following a quick exchange with Gonçalo Ramos before slotting the ball past Falcone.

Estupinan fired wide as the hosts looked to build on their lead, and just moments later Moreira scored their third goal of the evening.

The substitute won the ball just inside Lecce's half and raced down the left flank before cutting into the box, where he evaded the visiting defense and hit a low finish underneath Falcone in the 73rd minute.

Information from PA and The Associated Press was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Ravens preach team's resolve despite another collapse in 4th
articles.description: The Ravens did not want to draw parallels to past teams after Sunday's loss to the Saints despite losing in a similar manner with a fourth quarter lead.
articles.headlineJa: レイブンズ、第4クォーターで再び失速もチームの覚悟を主張
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズは日曜日のセインツ戦での敗戦後、第4クォーターのリードを守れず同様の形で敗れたものの、過去のチームと比較されることを望まなかった。
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- The Ravens didn't want to hear about their history of blowing fourth quarter leads after Sunday's 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints.

"Everybody's going to just say the same old thing of having a lead and things like that," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "So man, we will own this. We'll look in the mirror."

After leading 17-9 entering the fourth quarter, Baltimore gave up back-to-back, 68-yard touchdown drives to the Saints. The Ravens allowed the game-winning score with 1:28 remaining, when Saints quarterback Tyler Shough crossed the goal line on a 1-yard quarterback sneak.

Over the last six seasons, the Ravens have lost an NFL-worst 15 games when leading through three quarters.

"Our history is irrelevant to the future of where we want to go," Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell said. "It just comes down to how we respond and our execution going forward."

Once Minter replaced John Harbaugh after 18 seasons, his mantra became: "Be at our best, when our best is needed." But, on Sunday, Baltimore struggled late in the game like it had done so often under Harbaugh.

The Ravens, who led 14-3 late in the first half, lost for the 15th time after holding a double-digit lead since quarterback Lamar Jackson became the full-time starter in 2019. That's the most such losses by any team in the NFL over that span.

Tight end Mark Andrews doesn't believe you can compare this Ravens team to the ones in the past.

"I feel like this is a whole new team with a whole new energy," Andrews said. "These guys, this coaching staff, everybody -- there is not one similarity [that] I can feel. I feel like this team is built for adversity, built to get better [and] learn from our mistakes."

It looked like the Ravens were going to overcome the loss of No. 1 wide receiver Zay Flowers, who was out with a hamstring injury. In the first three quarters, Jackson was 18-of-24 (75%) for 207 yards and one touchdown.

In the fourth quarter, though, Jackson was 3-of-7 (42.9%) for 28 yards and an interception.

Jackson said there is no frustration in failing to finish in the fourth quarter again, saying, "Because I see where we can be. I see what we're capable of. I see it day in, day out."

On the final drive, Jackson drove the Ravens to the Saints' 37-yard line before he was picked off with 13 seconds remaining.

"I feel like I want that pass back," Jackson said.

Playing in their home opener, Minter opened his first team meeting last week talking about the importance of defending the home turf. Baltimore was 3-6 at M&T Bank Stadium last season, which was the worst home record in team history.

The Ravens have now lost four straight games at home, dating back to last season. This is one shy of tying the franchise record for futility at M&T Bank Stadium.

"It sucks," Ravens offensive tackle Roger Rosengarten said. "I can't remember the last time we won at home."

articles.headline: Hurts taunts Titans after Eagles win: Finished what you started
articles.description: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons approached Jalen Hurts for a post-game dap-up following Philadelphia's 24-20 come-from-behind win Sunday and the Eagles quarterback was ready for him.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルス勝利後にハーツがタイタンズを煽る：「自分たちが始めたことを終わらせただけだ」
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日、フィラデルフィアが24-20で逆転勝利を収めた後、テネシー・タイタンズのディフェンシブタックル、ジェフリー・シモンズが試合後の挨拶にジェイレン・ハーツへ近づくと、イーグルスのクォーターバックは彼を迎え撃つ準備ができていた。
articles.body:
NASHVILLE - Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons approached Jalen Hurts for a post-game dap-up following Philadelphia's 24-20 come-from-behind win Sunday and the Eagles quarterback was ready for him.

"You started that s---," Hurts said with a smile, taking a break from his postgame interview to address Simmons. "I had to finish it."

The two exchanged words after that but Hurts made it clear that he had heard Simmons' comments to reporters earlier in the week, when Simmons told reporters: "We just need to make Jalen Hurts be a QB. Stop his runs, make sure Hurts doesn't get out of the pocket and make plays."

Hurts got the last word, engineering a nine-play, 65-yard drive in the closing minutes and hitting receiver Darius Cooper for a three-yard touchdown pass with nine seconds remaining to lift the Eagles to a 2-0 record.

"I love our guys so of course my natural instinct is, 'Oh, I want to fight,'" said coach Nick Sirianni after the game. "But when you get wrapped into the battle of words or revenge or whatever it is, anger, that s--- lasts about two minutes in a game. It does. At the end of the day, the fundamentals take over, the situational awareness takes over, you playing together as a team, your toughness takes over, because that all fades."

Simmons added further context to his original comments postgame.

"He's a Super Bowl MVP," Simmons said. "That wasn't no shot at Jalen. The thing was if we could keep him in the pocket and eliminate him from scrambling and running, making him go sideways, we could be successful especially getting them to third down.

"We saw Jalen would try to make something happen downfield and take off running. You see it all over his tape. That was my point of making Jalen Hurts stay in the pocket and just be a quarterback. It wasn't, 'Oh he can't be a quarterback in the pocket.'"

Hurts and the offense were not having the best day at the office. The Eagles QB had thrown two interceptions, the operation looked sluggish at times minus running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) and behind a reconfigured offensive line working without left guard Landon Dickerson (knee). Tennessee went ahead by three on a field goal with six minutes remaining.

"Hey, let's finish. We've got them right where we want them," Hurts said before taking the field, according to Cooper.

Hurts went 5-of-7 on the final drive, including a 19-yarder to DeVonta Smith down the left sideline on 3rd-and-6 with 20 seconds remaining that put Philadelphia on the doorstep.

"He didn't flinch," Smith said of Hurts.

The next play was supposed to go to Smith as well, but the receiver lost his footing. Hurts' attention turned to Cooper, whose job was to run a pick for Smith on the play. He instead turned into the target and was able to haul in a high pass from Hurts in the back of the end zone. It was Cooper's first NFL touchdown and Hurts' first career go-ahead passing TD in the final minute of regulation or over

articles.headline: Arenado hits grand slam in the Diamondbacks' 8-4 victory over the Yankees
articles.description: — Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season top help the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 8-4 on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: アレナドが満塁ホームラン、ダイヤモンドバックスがヤンキースに8-4で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ノーラン・アレナドが今季3本目となる満塁ホームランを放ち、日曜日に行われた試合でアリゾナ・ダイヤモンドバックスが8-4でニューヨーク・ヤンキースを下すのに貢献した。
articles.body:
PHOENIX -- — Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season top help the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 8-4 on Sunday.


              Arenado connected off reliever Brent Headrick (7-4) in the fifth inning. The Diamondbacks loaded the bases against Yankee starter Will Warren when Headrick entered. He struck out Geraldo Perdomo for the second out but walked Corbin Carroll to force in a run before Arenado homered on a 2-1 pitch. He tied Houston’s Yordan Alvarez for the major league lead this season, and it was Arenado’s ninth career slam.


              The Diamondbacks had their MLB-best 47th comeback win of the season and kept pace with Philadelphia in the chase for the National League’s final wild-card berth, but trail the Phillies by four games with six to play.


              New York still has a slim chance to win the American League East, but must win out and get help. The Yankees open a four-game series Tuesday against the division-leading Rays in New York.


              Perdomo had a run-scoring single in the first and an RBI triple in the seventh.


              Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for New York, all in the third inning, off Arizona starter Corbin Burnes. 


              Justin Martinez (3-0) was one of five Arizona relievers to hold the Yankees to three hits in the final 6 1/3 innings.


              The Yankees finished their road season 47-34 (.580), second only to the Dodgers (46-32, .590). Arizona finished its home season 45-36 (.556), its best mark since 2017 (52-29, .642).


              Up next
              Yankees: Off Monday. Doubleheader at home against Tampa Bay on Tuesday with LHPs Carlos Rodón (6-3, 2.95 ERA) and Max Fried (5-4. 2.63) set to start for New York against RHPs Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) and Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72).


              Diamondbacks: Off Monday. RHP Michael Soroka (8-5, 3.45) was scheduled to start Tuesday at Colorado against LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.38).


              ------
